chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A female hairdresser came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said to her: 'Have you left your work or are you still established upon it?' She said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I do it unless you forbid me from it, so I shall refrain from it.' He said to her: 'Do it. But when you comb hair, do not polish the face with the rag, for it removes the water of the face, and do not attach the hair with the hair.'

key_terms.الْخِرَقِ: Rag or cloth used for polishing

ai.seo_question: What are the specific professional etiquettes for female hairdressers mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the permissibility of female hairdressing as a legitimate profession, provided it adheres to specific hygienic and ritual purity standards. The Prophet’s (peace be upon him) instruction to avoid removing facial moisture (likely referring to sweat or natural oils essential for purity) and to prevent mixing hairs underscores the integration of practical trade ethics with Islamic jurisprudence, a key theme in Shia legal tradition regarding women's economic participation.
